params.body:
The next event sat under the hero as one small italic line ("vr 30 okt" plus the title in body text) and was easy to miss. It now gets a band of its own.

## What changes

- A full-width bone band between the hero and the photo, with the next event as a calendar sheet: weekday on an oxblood strip, the day large in Cormorant, the month below.
- Title in the display face, sized by length with the same `titleLength()` steps as the agenda; time and admission on one line; summary only when it does not repeat the title; an "Alle info" link. The whole block links to the event page.
- Further featured or upcoming events follow as short lines under it.
- The side quote, when set in the homepage document, still shows under the buttons; it no longer hides the events.

## Staying current on a static site

The page is built ahead of time, so a small inline script runs in the visitor's browser:

- the label above the title becomes "Vanavond", "Vandaag", "Morgen", "Over N dagen" or "Nu bezig" (days counted in Brussels time), and stays "Binnenkort" further out or without JavaScript;
- events that are over (after `endsAt`, or six hours after the start when there is no end) are removed, and the band disappears when none are left.

## Checked

- `astro build` against the live dataset (read only) and `tsc --noEmit`, both clean.
- Desktop (1440) and phone (390) screenshots of the band with the live opening event; the label read "Morgen" on 29 October.
- Not seen rendered: the list of further events, since the dataset holds one upcoming event.
params.title: Home: show the next event as a featured band
